assertions.description: SVGPathElement.prototype exposes getPathData as a function.
SVGPathElement.prototype exposes setPathData as a function.
SVGPathElement.prototype exposes getPathSegmentAtLength as a function.
getPathData() returns an array of plain {type, values} segment objects matching the authored commands.
assertions.test: (() => { if (!('getPathData' in SVGPathElement.prototype)) return false; const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); p.setAttribute('d', 'M 0 0 L 10 10'); const d = p.getPathData(); return Array.isArray(d) && d.length === 2 && d[0].type === 'M' && Array.isArray(d[0].values) && d[0].values.length === 2 && d[1].type === 'L'; })()

assertions.description: A raw getPathData() read preserves relative and shorthand commands (h stays h, q stays q) rather than normalizing them.
assertions.test: (() => { if (!('getPathData' in SVGPathElement.prototype)) return false; const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); p.setAttribute('d', 'M 10 10 h 40 q 20 30 40 0'); const t = p.getPathData().map((s) => s.type).join(''); return t === 'Mhq'; })()

assertions.description: getPathData({normalize: true}) reduces every command (relative, H/V, quadratic, arc) to absolute M, L, C or Z.
assertions.test: (() => { if (!('getPathData' in SVGPathElement.prototype)) return false; const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); p.setAttribute('d', 'M 10 10 h 40 V 60 q 20 30 40 0 a 10 10 0 0 1 10 10 Z'); const n = p.getPathData({ normalize: true }); return n.length > 0 && n.every((s) => s.type === 'M' || s.type === 'L' || s.type === 'C' || s.type === 'Z'); })()

assertions.description: setPathData() accepts plain {type, values} objects, writes a non-empty d attribute, and the written path reads back with the same commands and values (the serialization's exact whitespace is not part of the contract).
assertions.test: (() => { if (!('setPathData' in SVGPathElement.prototype) || !('getPathData' in SVGPathElement.prototype)) return false; const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); p.setPathData([{ type: 'M', values: [0, 0] }, { type: 'L', values: [50, 50] }]); const d = p.getAttribute('d'); if (typeof d !== 'string' || d.length === 0) return false; const back = p.getPathData(); return back.length === 2 && back[0].type === 'M' && back[0].values[0] === 0 && back[0].values[1] === 0 && back[1].type === 'L' && back[1].values[0] === 50 && back[1].values[1] === 50; })()

assertions.description: getPathData() on a path with no d attribute returns an empty array, not null and not an exception.
assertions.test: (() => { if (!('getPathData' in SVGPathElement.prototype)) return false; const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); const d = p.getPathData(); return Array.isArray(d) && d.length === 0; })()

assertions.description: getPathSegmentAtLength(NaN) throws a TypeError: the distance argument is a restricted float, so NaN and infinities are rejected before the lookup runs.
assertions.test: (() => { if (!('getPathSegmentAtLength' in SVGPathElement.prototype)) return false; const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); p.setAttribute('d', 'M 0 0 L 10 0'); try { p.getPathSegmentAtLength(NaN); return false; } catch (error) { return error instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: A negative distance clamps to 0, which falls exactly on the boundary between the zero-length moveto and the first lineto, and the spec requires the later segment: L with values [10, 0].
assertions.test: (() => { if (!('getPathSegmentAtLength' in SVGPathElement.prototype)) return false; const p = document.createElementNS('http://www.w3.org/2000/svg', 'path'); p.setAttribute('d', 'M 0 0 L 10 0 L 10 10'); const s = p.getPathSegmentAtLength(-5); return s !== null && s.type === 'L' && Array.isArray(s.values) && s.values.length === 2 && s.values[0] === 10 && s.values[1] === 0; })()
